title: Elastic Fidelity Debt Amortization — Operational Playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the Elastic Fidelity Debt Amortization pattern: a deterministic, observable procedure to reduce latency/cost SLO debt by gradually stepping application fidelity (model variant, quantization, batch sizing, caching aggressiveness) using a staircase profile. The goal is to preserve user-facing availability while amortizing the operational and quality cost of emergency fidelity drops over a controlled time window.

When to use
-----------
- High short-term load or capacity pressure where immediate full-fidelity fallback causes unacceptable cost or instability.
- Post-incident recovery when we want to converge back to nominal fidelity without causing new tail-latency spikes.
- Release windows for quantization/kernel rollouts where a fast rollback would cause excess cost or churn.

Intended guarantees and SLOs impacted
------------------------------------
- Availability: no more than 1% user-facing errors during transition windows.
- Latency: p95 should remain below configured emergency SLO (example: 450ms).
- Quality budget: aggregated eval-score degradation limited to -3% per 10 minutes during amortization.
- Cost smoothing: avoid >2x immediate per-token cost increase when restoring fidelity.

Key concepts and terminology
----------------------------
- Fidelity Step: a named configuration applying a set of runtime knobs (model_variant, quant_profile, batch_max, kvcache_mode, kernel_variant).
- Debt Window: the time budget to recover (e.g., 30m).
- Amortization Staircase: ordered fidelity steps applied at deterministic intervals.
- Safety Gate: quality and latency checks that must pass before launching the next step up.

Example Staircase (recommended baseline)
---------------------------------------
1) emergency-low: small quantized variant, aggressive batch coalescing, KV cache only prefix mode. (immediate)
2) safety-hold: medium quantized variant, conservative batch increase, KV caching warmed, kernel spec fallback. (+5 minutes)
3) gradual-restore-1: larger variant with per-tenant token cap lift, reduced quantization. (+10 minutes)
4) gradual-restore-2: near-nominal variant, speculative prefetching enabled. (+20 minutes)
5) nominal: full-fidelity model variant and runtime knobs. (+30–60 minutes)

Operational configuration (policy sample YAML)
--------------------------------------------
- name: elastic_fidelity_amortization
  debt_window_minutes: 30
  steps:
    - id: emergency-low
      duration_minutes: 5
      model_variant: "gptx-mini-q4"
      quant_profile: "q4-agg"
      batch_max_tokens: 1024
      kvcache_mode: "prefix-only"
      accept_quality_drop_pct: 5.0
    - id: safety-hold
      duration_minutes: 5
      model_variant: "gptx-small-q4"
      quant_profile: "q4"
      batch_max_tokens: 2048
      kvcache_mode: "normal"
      accept_quality_drop_pct: 3.0
    - id: gradual-restore-1
      duration_minutes: 10
      model_variant: "gptx-base-q8"
      quant_profile: "q8"
      batch_max_tokens: 3072
      kvcache_mode: "normal-warmup"
      accept_quality_drop_pct: 1.5
    - id: nominal
      duration_minutes: 10
      model_variant: "gptx-base"
      quant_profile: "fp16"
      batch_max_tokens: 4096
      kvcache_mode: "full"
      accept_quality_drop_pct: 0.2

Telemetry signals to watch (real-time)
-------------------------------------
- runtime.p95_ms (by route and model_variant) — target: < emergency_slo_ms
- runtime.error_rate (5m rolling) — immediate abort threshold: >1%
- runtime.kvcache_hit_ratio (by tenant) — expected to increase through steps; flag if < 20% after step 2
- cost.per_1k_tokens (approx) — should not spike >2x baseline when moving steps
- eval_shadow.delta_score (shadow eval harness) — must stay within accept_quality_drop_pct

Runbook: emergency execution (operator path)
-------------------------------------------
1) Detect: Pager triggers (high p95 or GPU OOM alerts). Open incident in Slack channel #runtime-incidents and create an incident stub.
2) Immediate action (0–2 min): set policy to emergency-low. CLI: redwood runtime apply-policy --policy elastic_fidelity_amortization --start-step emergency-low --force
3) Observe (2–7 min): watch runtime.p95_ms, runtime.error_rate, kvcache_hit_ratio. If error_rate >1.5% after emergency-low, escalate to oncall and consider capacity-side mitigations (resume fallback region or scale up dedicated capacity).
4) Controlled staircase (5–30 min): allow policy to advance per configured durations. Before each advance, execute Safety Gate checks (see below). If a gate fails, halt and execute remedial actions (warm caches/evict/prefetch or re-enforce batching).
5) Converge to nominal: once nominal step passes all gates for two consecutive intervals, mark incident resolved and create a post-incident note with metric deltas.

Safety Gate checks (pre-step promotion)
--------------------------------------
- Promoted if:
  - p95 improved or stable (within 10% of previous step)
  - error_rate <= 1%
  - shadow eval delta_score >= -accept_quality_drop_pct for step
  - no GPU OOMs in the past 3m
- If any check fails, run corrective sequence:
  - run: redwood runtime profile-collect --tenant <T> --duration 60s --tags step-promote
  - increase kvcache prefetch multiplier: redwood runtime set-kvcache --prefetch-multiplier 2 --tenant <T>
  - re-run safety gate after 2 minutes

Automated validation (CI gating)
-------------------------------
Before enabling Elastic Fidelity in production for a route, the following automated checks must pass in the staging environment:
- Ladder replay: run end-to-end request replay for 30 minutes covering the staircase transitions and verify p95 and error_rate projections.
- Shadow-eval: run prompt set shadow evaluation across steps and ensure aggregated delta_score within configured accept thresholds.
- Kernel compatibility test: validate kernel_variant fallbacks do not raise lane-level tail latencies beyond 25% of baseline.

Testing checklist (on-call drills)
----------------------------------
- Create a synthetic overcapacity event using the operational workload simulator and run the full amortization staircase in sandbox.
- Validate metrics ingestion and dashboarding for the key signals above.
- Time-boxed rollback: practice invoking immediate revert to nominal-low-cost fallback and verify rollback completes in < 60s.

Rollbacks and aborts
--------------------
- Immediate rollback: CLI: redwood runtime apply-policy --policy elastic_fidelity_amortization --start-step nominal --force
- Partial abort: set --hold-on-step <id> to prevent promotions while investigating.
- If operator cannot recover within debt_window_minutes, escalate to platform oncall for capacity scaling and perform emergency region failover if configured.

Ownership and handoff
---------------------
- Primary owners: runtime-operator (oncall rotation) and scheduling team (for kernel_variant toggles).
- Post-incident: assign a runbook owner to update policy thresholds and record lessons in the incident postmortem.

Observability and dashboards (recommended panels)
------------------------------------------------
- Elastic Fidelity Console: composite view showing current step per route, time-in-step, and per-step telemetry deltas.
- Step health chart: p95 / error_rate / kvcache_hit_ratio overlayed with step annotations.
- Shadow-eval trend: rolling delta_score for top 100 prompts.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets
----------------------------
- Show active policy and current step:
  redwood runtime get-policy --name elastic_fidelity_amortization --format table

- Force start a specific step:
  redwood runtime apply-policy --policy elastic_fidelity_amortization --start-step safety-hold --reason \"operator emergency\"

- Collect a 60s trace for step-promote troubleshooting:
  redwood runtime profile-collect --route <route> --duration 60s --output /tmp/trace.json

- Example alert rule (Prometheus):
  ALERT ElasticFidelityErrorSpike
    IF increase(runtime_error_total[2m]) > 0.01
    FOR 5m
    LABELS {severity=\"critical\"}
    ANNOTATIONS {summary=\"Error rate spike during amortization\"}

Notes and rationale
-------------------
- Why amortize? Immediate full-quality restores create hot-path costs and may re-trigger capacity instability. Gradual promotion reduces sudden spikes, lets caches warm, and provides measurable quality checkpoints.
- Why deterministic staircase? Human-friendly timeboxes improve predictability for oncall and allow automation to assert safety gates.
